name: UI feedback duration
statement: UI feedback animates between 150 and 300ms; modals and drawers may take up to 500ms.
source: Material Design 3 motion duration guidance, cross-checked against WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3

name: Decorative loop budget
statement: At most two infinite decorative loops per view, each guarded for reduced motion.
source: NullToHero editorial: restraint budget, no external source

name: Scrub easing
statement: Scrubbed tweens use linear easing; perceived easing comes from the visitor's scroll.
source: Parallax practice: a scroll-linked tween must not ease, or it lags the finger

name: Tap target size
statement: Tap targets clear 24 by 24 CSS pixels, the WCAG 2.5.8 AA conformance floor; 44 by 44 is the recommended comfort target on touch.
source: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), AA

name: Target spacing
statement: Adjacent tap targets keep at least 8px of separation.
source: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 spacing exception

name: Referenced video budget
statement: Referenced video stays under 10 MB; 30 MB is the hard failure line.
source: NullToHero editorial: mobile data budget

name: 3D model budget
statement: A 3D model stays under 5 MB or ships Draco/meshopt compression.
source: NullToHero editorial: hero video budget

name: Frame sequence staging
statement: Fifty-plus eagerly loaded sequential frames is a burst; stage in a window around the scroll position.
source: NullToHero editorial: image-sequence memory budget

name: Body size
statement: Base body text is at least 16px.
source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.4 plus common mobile reading practice

name: Measure
statement: Body line length sits between 45 and 75 characters, with 65 to 75 the optimal band.
source: Typographic convention: Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style

name: Text contrast
statement: Body text hits 4.5:1 against its background; 3:1 for large or bold-large text.
source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), AA

name: LCP
statement: Largest Contentful Paint under 2.5 seconds on a mid-range mobile.
source: Google Core Web Vitals thresholds, web.dev/lcp

name: CLS
statement: Cumulative Layout Shift under 0.1.
source: Google Core Web Vitals thresholds, web.dev/cls

name: INP
statement: Interaction to Next Paint under 200ms at p75.
source: Google Core Web Vitals thresholds, web.dev/inp

name: Draw call ceiling
statement: A WebGL scene aims for a few hundred draw calls and never exceeds 1000; instancing beyond.
source: three.js performance guidance plus the plugin's own measurements

name: Pixel ratio cap
statement: Renderer pixel ratio is capped at 2.
source: three.js WebGLRenderer.setPixelRatio guidance

name: Editorial quality gate
statement: Composite editorial quality reaches 70 out of 100 before publication, on the five weighted dimensions.
source: NullToHero editorial: content score pass mark

name: Sentence rhythm
statement: Sentence-length standard deviation sits between 8 and 15 words, peaking near 10; flat rhythm is the most reliable tell of unedited generation.
source: NullToHero editorial, derived from the slop-pattern corpus

name: Prose to structure balance
statement: Between half and three quarters of a document is prose; over-listing is penalised harder than under-listing.
source: NullToHero editorial, derived from the slop-pattern corpus

name: Keyword density ceiling
statement: Main keyword occupies under 3 percent of the words, measured as words covered by matches and not as occurrences over word count.
source: SEO practice: density above this reads as stuffing to every current engine

name: Tier 1 AI crawler access
statement: Every tier 1 AI crawler reaches the site; a blocked search or user fetcher costs citations, unlike a blocked training crawler.
source: NullToHero editorial: AI crawler access policy

name: Crawler access is HTTP-level
statement: Bot user-agents receive the same HTTP status as a browser; robots.txt states intent and the edge decides outcome.
source: NullToHero editorial: rendered parity requirement

name: Aligned comparison windows
statement: Two compared periods are of strictly equal length and end at least three days back, because Search Console has no data for the current day.
source: Search Console export semantics

name: Refusal to score
statement: No numeric score is emitted for a dimension with fewer than half its inputs available; report insufficient data instead.
source: NullToHero editorial: audit coverage floor

name: Full-bleed viewport unit
statement: A full-bleed section that must never reveal the page behind it is sized in dvh; svh stops growing when the phone browser bar retracts and leaves a band of page background.
source: CSS Values 4 dynamic viewport units, and iOS Safari toolbar behaviour

name: Viewport unit consistency
statement: A pinned scroll track and the platter pinned inside it use the same viewport unit; mixing vh and svh retimes every act because the two resolve to different heights.
source: NullToHero editorial: one scroll system per page

name: Programmatic page-count gates
statement: Below 100 generated pages standard practice applies; 100 to 499 is a warning and takes a 10 percent sample audit; 500 to 4999 is a high alert and takes a full quality audit; 5000 and above is a hard stop until a thin-content prevention plan exists. Four tiers, not two: collapsing them relabels the alert as the stop.
source: NullToHero editorial: programmatic page-count thresholds

name: Location page gates
statement: Location pages gate harder than generic programmatic pages, warning at 30 and hard stop at 50 without a thin-content audit, because a city-templated set is the canonical doorway pattern and the same page count carries more risk.
source: NullToHero editorial: local page-count thresholds

name: Page-type word floors
statement: Per-page-type word counts are topical coverage floors and never targets. The single table lives in content.md and is cited; restating a different number elsewhere is how three files came to disagree on the same product page.
source: NullToHero editorial: minimum word counts live in one table

name: IndexNow participant list
statement: The IndexNow participant list is stated once, with a date, in indexnow.md. No other file enumerates it, because a partial copy does not look stale when a participant joins, it just stays quietly wrong.
source: IndexNow participant list, one dated table in indexnow.md

name: Consecutive build difference
statement: Two consecutive builds in a project log differ on at least two of paper band, display family, accent hue and colour strategy, and at least one of those two is paper or display. Hue and coverage can both move without the page looking different; the surface and the display face are what a reader sees first.
source: NullToHero editorial: build variety predicate

name: Page shape repeat window
statement: A page shape is not reused inside the last three builds recorded in LOG.md. Three is enough to stop the drift toward one default shape without forbidding a shape the project genuinely needs twice.
source: NullToHero editorial: shape repeat window

name: Narrowest supported viewport
statement: Entrance and exit travel is expressed relative to the element, and any absolute translate is measured against 375px, the narrowest viewport the plugin supports. A percentage moves the element by its own size and is safe everywhere; a pixel length is a bet on the reader's screen.
source: Narrowest viewport the plugin supports; matches the 375px iPhone SE class

name: Per-item stagger delay
statement: A list or grid staggers its items by 40 to 80ms each. Below 40 the sequence reads as simultaneous and the stagger buys nothing; above 80 the last item makes the reader wait. The value was contested across five references (30-50, 30-80, 40-80, 50-100, 100-150) and is settled here on motion-choreography.md, whose subject is choreography and whose figure is the middle of the observed range.
source: NullToHero editorial, settled from five contradicting references (see P8)

name: Exit to entrance duration ratio
statement: An exit runs at 75% of its entrance duration. Leaving should feel quicker than arriving, and a single ratio keeps a system coherent. Four references said 75% and one said 60 to 70%; the majority holds and the outlier is corrected rather than averaged.
source: NullToHero editorial, majority of four references against one outlier (see P8)
